question: Should OpenClaw preserve strict deny-on-unresolved approvals as the only execution-authorizing outcome, or add a separately named, non-authorizing advisory timeout outcome for plugin-initiated gates?
rationale: The current public contract intentionally ignores legacy `timeoutBehavior: "allow"`, while a recent dependent workflow asks for explicit advisory semantics; choosing that permanent authority boundary cannot safely be inferred from code alone. ([docs.openclaw.ai](https://docs.openclaw.ai/plugins/hooks?utm_source=openai))

options.title: Keep fail-closed authorization
options.body: Keep unresolved approvals deny-only and scope any advisory workflow as a separate non-authorizing plugin capability, with the API direction handled in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/97043.

options.title: Add an explicit advisory outcome
options.body: Define a narrowly scoped plugin API whose timeout outcome is recorded distinctly and cannot be mistaken for execution authorization, with contract, migration, and security review.

recommendation.title: Keep fail-closed authorization
recommendation.body: Keep unresolved approvals deny-only and scope any advisory workflow as a separate non-authorizing plugin capability, with the API direction handled in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/97043.
